# Attribution — FinderRight single-catalog and editor-catalog reference

**No FinderRight source is vendored.** Nothing in this directory is a copy, a
transliteration, or a partial extract of funny-dog/FinderRight, and no file in
CrossOS is derived from its text. This entry records a behaviour reference and
is the evidence that a structural port was made rather than a copy.

Source repository: funny-dog/FinderRight
Source commit: af8d5f0fe2479e3d1b0afc7d01829feb0e022910
Source file: FinderRightKit/Sources/FinderRightKit/MenuFeature.swift:3-6 and FinderRightKit/Sources/FinderRightKit/EditorCatalog.swift:16-19
Original license: MIT
Original copyright: Copyright (c) 2026 FinderRight
CrossOS destination: core/cmd/crossos/findermenu.go (handleFinderMenuEntries and finderFileType) + core/cmd/crossos/finderdata.go (menuRows and menuUnavailableReason — the page-side half of the same one list, and the sentences it prints beside a row that cannot run)
Modification: structural port, no code copied. What transfers is the rule the reference states about itself in Chinese and then keeps: MenuFeature.swift:3-6 calls a menu item 全应用的「单一事实来源」— the single source of truth for the whole app — because "两端共用同一份清单与同一套 id，避免「设置里的开关与右键菜单对不上」": the main app's settings screen and the FinderSync extension share ONE list and ONE set of ids, precisely so the toggle in Settings cannot disagree with the menu in the right-click. CrossOS had exactly that disagreement. handleFinderMenuEntries read filetype.Seeds(), so the appex's New submenu carried whatever the shipped catalog enabled — one row — no matter what a person switched on in the Explorer page. It now reads the same c.set.FileTypes() the page writes. finderFileType is changed in the same commit because it resolved createFile's extension from the same seeds: fixing only the reader would put a row in the submenu that the verb it fires then refuses, which is the submenu entry that fails on click.
Reason for modification: medium and language port — a Swift struct with localized name keys becomes a Go handler reading one store. The 🟡 behaviour-only grade for FinderRight is in §9.3's licence table (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md:1149), NOT in §9.10: that section states the per-file copy contract and carries no FinderRight row, and §9.11 grades no FinderRight entry either. This entry was cross-referenced to §9.10 before; the grade is recorded here at the section that actually carries it. FinderRight is in no P0 list (§9.9), in no file-level reuse row (§9.10) and in no direct-reuse grade (§9.11), so it is behaviour-only by DEFAULT — an ungraded repository is not a copy target — rather than by a table verdict. That is the narrower claim this block is entitled to make, and it is the one it makes: the single-catalog RULE, cited line by line, and not the code. EditorCatalog.swift:16-19 contributes the ORDER rule — the order of the list is the order the submenu shows — but NOT its installed-filter, which the extension applies at display time with NSWorkspace; CrossOS serves no way to enumerate installed editors, so the honest port keeps the ordering and leaves the filter as a stated gap rather than inventing a stand-in. The two sentences menuUnavailableReason prints beside a row that cannot run — a capability the intent registry has no row for, and an adapter that only runs on macOS (finderdata.go:105-123) — are NOT ports, and this entry does not claim them: FinderRight has no referent for either. It decides availability per context and OMITS what cannot run (FinderSync.swift:147-148 — '功能开关：默认开启，用户在设置里关闭后对应菜单项隐藏', the featureOn guard in front of every addItem at :155-197); it greys exactly one item and says nothing about why (:180-183, pasteItem.isEnabled = hasCut, carrying no tooltip and no caption); and its settings row is a plain always-enabled Toggle with no availability concept at all (FeatureToggleRow.swift:9-11), the only prose about the off state being one global footer (SettingsView.swift:175, '关闭的功能不会出现在 Finder 右键菜单中'). CrossOS goes the other way and keeps the row, greys it, prints the reason beside it and leaves it turnable (finderdata.go:131-152) — a deliberate divergence that costs a person less, since the sentence says which host refuses and what would change that. The single-catalog rule is what makes the question answerable at all: one list and one id means the page's verdict and the appex's menu are one fact about one host, so the reason and the boolean are asked of one function rather than two that can disagree (finderdata.go:53-61, :76-84). The words are CrossOS's own, about CrossOS's own dispatch table.
